clue.text: The periphrasis "abstaining from skating" was invented by 1 down

parts.note: periphrasis is roundabout speech, saying things the long way round
someone who is not on the rink is off the ice, read as two words

explanation.surface: Someone credits a famous novelist with coining a fancy phrase for not skating.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 down is CHARLES DICKENS, whose Little Dorrit satirises a government department of this name that exists to avoid getting anything done.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional obstructive government department is Dickens's creation in the novel Little Dorrit.

clue.text: Author of "Roald's Birds" (Spooner)

indicators.note: the reference to the Reverend Spooner says the opening sounds of two words are to be swapped

parts.note: Roald Dahl, the children's author, so Roald's suggests Dahl's
chickens are birds

explanation.surface: An imaginary book title about birds belonging to a famous children's writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of DAHL'S CHICKENS and you hear the novelist's name; the swap works by sound, not spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian novelist of Oliver Twist is a classic example of an author.

clue.text: A circle in the list indicates a bird

indicators.note: the circle sits inside the list, so in signals one piece placed within another

parts.note: a roster is a list of names, as for duties
O is the shape of a circle

explanation.surface: A ring drawn on a checklist marks out one particular bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel, the male domestic fowl, is a bird.

clue.text: Beast overcomes alien in "Talk of the Town"

indicators.note: the beast and alien are placed inside the talk, so in signals containment

parts.note: to utter is to talk or say

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece over another means it comes first, on top

parts.note: an ox is a beast of burden
ET is the film alien, the Extra-Terrestrial

explanation.surface: A monster defeats an extraterrestrial and becomes the talk of the town.
explanation.walkthrough: UTTOXETER is a market town in Staffordshire, England; 'Talk of the Town' looks like a phrase but splits into fodder and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Staffordshire place with a famous racecourse is a market town.

clue.text: Tailless predator that flies round America goes to European city

indicators.note: the shortened falcon goes round the country, so round signals one piece enclosing another
the bird loses its tail, meaning its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a lanner is a kind of falcon, a bird of prey
USA is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A bird of prey without its tail travels across America and on to a city in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailless' docks the falcon's last letter, giving LANNE; 'flies' tempts a solver to think of insects, but the predator is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss city on Lake Geneva is in Europe.

clue.text: Nibble has primate power?

parts.note: can expresses having the power or ability to do something
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A question whether a snack gives monkey strength.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'has primate power' as 'can ape', that is, is able to copy, which joins into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A small savoury on bread or pastry served with drinks is a nibble.

clue.text: Rescue vehicle sometimes of ivory?

definitions.meaning: a breakdown truck is something that tows, a tow truck
an ivory ... is a place of detached academic seclusion

explanation.definitionFit: A tow truck pulls broken cars; a tall building can be made of ivory in the idiom.

clue.text: Skip around capital — no time for paperwork

indicators.note: no time says the letter for time is removed
skip goes round the capital, so around signals enclosure

parts.note: to omit something is to skip it
Riga is the capital of Latvia

explanation.surface: Someone skips around a capital city with no time for their administrative chores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' builds ORIGAMIT, and 'no time' then strips its T; the dash makes 'paperwork' look like office drudgery rather than folding.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese art of folding paper is literally work with paper.

clue.text: If we can, each blighted noun must be translated — if only!

indicators.note: translating renders words into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A frustrated wish that every damaged noun could be put into another language.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is 'must be translated'; 'blighted' looks like it could be one, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a wistful remark meaning one wishes something were possible.

clue.text: It's a volte-face to call a fight entertainment

parts.note: a bout is a fight, as in boxing
a turn is a performer's act in a variety show

explanation.surface: Describing a boxing match as a show is a complete reversal of opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete reversal of direction or opinion is an about-face, a military-style turn.

clue.text: Spellbinder's report for magazine

indicators.note: a report is a sound, so the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a witch casts spells, binding people

explanation.surface: A sorcerer's write-up appears in a periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: Which? is a British consumer magazine that tests products.
explanation.definitionFit: The consumer magazine published by the Consumers' Association is a magazine title.

clue.text: Not strict about note for getting rubber

indicators.note: lax goes round the note, so about signals enclosing

parts.note: lax means not strict
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A lenient attitude to a musical note somehow yields rubber.
explanation.definitionFit: The milky sap of rubber trees, or synthetic material like it, is a form of rubber.

clue.text: Be related to a fixer by acknowledgment being inserted

indicators.note: the two pieces are put into the fixer, so being inserted signals containment

parts.note: a pin fixes things together
per means by, as in per post
ta is British informal thanks, an acknowledgment

explanation.surface: Someone is linked to a repairman by a word of thanks slipped in.
explanation.definitionFit: To pertain or belong to something is to be related to it.

clue.text: Report of wage much below minimum requires investigation

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the phrase is said aloud

parts.note: screw is British slang for wages, and a tiny one is far below the minimum

explanation.surface: News of a pitiful wage demands an inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screw' meaning pay is old British slang; 'screw tiny' said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Close critical examination is a form of investigation.

clue.text: See 1
See 8
Message for vehicle going round Eastern part of course

indicators.note: the vehicle goes round the other pieces, so they sit inside it

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle
a leg is one stage of a course or journey

explanation.surface: A note sent for a tram going around the eastern part of its route.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegraphed communication is a message.

clue.text: Congenital idiot starts taking note round the fleet

indicators.note: the start of idiot means its first letter

parts.note: NB is nota bene, a written note
O is round in shape
RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's fleet

explanation.surface: A born fool begins to take notice as the navy sails round.
explanation.definitionFit: Inborn and congenital both describe qualities present from birth: synonyms.

clue.text: Optimistic president conceals mounting misfortune

indicators.note: the president hides the other piece within him, so conceals signals containment

parts.note: Bush was the name of two US presidents

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means going upwards, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: an ill is a misfortune or trouble

explanation.surface: A hopeful head of state hides growing troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' makes LLI, since a down clue is read upward; 'Optimistic' fits the stock-market sense of a bull.
explanation.definitionFit: On the stock market a bull expects rising prices, so the related adjective means optimistic.

clue.text: Artist's cat receiving unction and love

indicators.note: the cat takes on the following pieces after it

parts.note: Leo is the lion, a big cat
nard, or spikenard, is an aromatic ointment used for anointing
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A painter's cat is given ointment and affection.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Artist's' stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Da Vinci, painter of the Mona Lisa, is a supreme artist.

clue.text: One murmuring quietly during check on queen

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above the next piece
quietly falls within the check, so during signals insertion

parts.note: a rein checks a horse
p is the musical marking piano, meaning quietly
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles under their breath while keeping a watch on the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To repine is to fret or complain, so one who does this murmurs discontent.

clue.text: Singular situation of 3 on a Scottish island

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: 3 down is a town in Staffordshire, abbreviated Staffs; made singular it loses the S

explanation.surface: A unique place for a town sits on a Scottish isle.
explanation.walkthrough: Staffordshire, a county in central England, is written Staffs; 'Singular' drops the plural-looking S.
explanation.definitionFit: The small Hebridean isle with Fingal's Cave lies off western Scotland.

clue.text: Fate (see replacing pole) relating to distance

indicators.note: one piece takes the place of another, signalling a substitution

parts.note: kismet is fate or destiny
S is the South pole
lo means see, as in lo and behold
re means about or relating to

explanation.surface: A bracketed remark about destiny concerns how far away something is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' gives KILOMET; the brackets make 'see replacing pole' look like an aside, but it is the working.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand metres is a unit of distance.

clue.text: Article of 1049 featuring 19?

parts.note: in Roman numerals M is 1000 and IL is a loose way of writing 49
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A news item from the eleventh century featuring a famous painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 across painted The Last Supper in a convent refectory in this city, so it features him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian city holds Da Vinci's Last Supper mural, so it features that artist's work.

clue.text: Characteristic of "Planty" Palliser

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the phrase, so of signals a run inside it

explanation.surface: A trait typical of a fictional Palliser nicknamed Planty.
explanation.walkthrough: Plantagenet Palliser is a politician in Trollope's Palliser novels, so the nickname looks natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Typal means typical, characteristic of a type.

clue.text: Educationalist, one partly Summerhill's finisher

indicators.note: only part of the word one is used, its closing letters
the finish of the school name means its closing letters

explanation.surface: An educator who is partly responsible for the end of Summerhill.
explanation.walkthrough: A. S. Neill founded Summerhill, the progressive English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: A. S. Neill was a Scottish educator, the founder of Summerhill school.

clue.text: One at cribbage, if honourable brothers make it

indicators.note: the pieces are made into a new arrangement, so make it signals rearranging

explanation.surface: Distinguished siblings score a point in a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: In cribbage, a card game popular in British pubs, holding the jack of the turned-up suit scores one point under this phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the single point scored at cribbage for holding the right jack.

clue.text: Illusory series about an atom is a graph

indicators.note: the letters are moved about, so about signals an anagram

explanation.surface: A sequence of illusions concerning an atom turns out to be a chart.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamlike sequence of shifting images is an illusory series.
